title: KPIRow
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid with two GridItem(.flexible()) columns (one at accessibility text sizes), or ScrollView(.horizontal) with LazyHStack, containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal, count:span:spacing:), scrollTargetLayout() and scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned); accessibilityElement(children: .contain) with accessibilityLabel names the row
summary: A recipe, not a component: the row of key figures at the top of a dashboard, as MonarchStatCards in a two-column grid or in a sideways row that snaps card by card, with one loading and error state for the whole row.
whenToUse: At the top of a dashboard or a report screen, for three to six figures with their change against the previous period.
whenNotToUse: For a single figure use MonarchStatCard on its own. For figures that belong to one record use LabeledContent with the Monarch style. For a trend over time use a chart.
api: LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: theme.spacing.space3), count: dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 1 : 2), spacing: theme.spacing.space3) { MonarchStatCard(…) }

ScrollView(.horizontal) { LazyHStack(spacing: theme.spacing.space3) { MonarchStatCard(…).containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal, count: 5, span: 4, spacing: theme.spacing.space3) }.scrollTargetLayout() }.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
MonarchStatCard(_:value:isLoading: true) for each placeholder; MonarchInlineErrorRetry(_:variant: .banner, onRetry:) in place of the row

options.name: columns
options.description: Two on a phone, one at accessibility text sizes; an iPad layout can use GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:)) for as many as fit.

options.name: scroll
options.description: Keeps one row: each card takes four fifths of the width so the next one shows, and scrolling stops on a card.

options.name: size / variant
options.description: Passed to every MonarchStatCard: .sm for dense rows, .lg for a hero row, .plain inside another card.

options.name: loading
options.description: Every card's isLoading; with no figures yet, four placeholder cards labelled Loading.

options.name: error
options.description: Replaces the row with MonarchInlineErrorRetry in its banner variant.

options.name: label
options.description: Names the group for VoiceOver, for example This month.

states.name: ready
states.description: The cards with their values, changes and sparklines.

states.name: loading
states.description: Each card shows its own loading placeholder; with no figures yet, placeholder cards keep the row's height.

states.name: error
states.description: One banner with Try again in place of the row, not an error per card.

states.name: scrolling
states.description: A sideways row that stops on each card, with the next card partly visible.

appearance: Every part is MonarchStatCard: the surface, border, value, change and sparkline in their roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow. Cards are spaced by space3.
platformNotes: The web ships KPIRow as a component over StatCardGroup with columns, minItemWidth, overflow, loading and error props. On iOS it is a recipe: a LazyVGrid or a snapping horizontal ScrollView already lays out the cards, and MonarchStatCard owns the loading, error and value states, so a wrapper would only rename SwiftUI's layout parameters. The web's minItemWidth breakpoint becomes two columns on a phone and one at accessibility text sizes; its overflow scroll becomes scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), the system's snapping. The web's role group with aria-label is an accessibility container with a label. The web makes a scrolling row a tab stop for the keyboard; on iOS the scroll view scrolls with swipes and VoiceOver moves into it card by card. Android has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The row is a container named by its label, so VoiceOver says This month when it moves into it.
Each card keeps MonarchStatCard's reading: label, value and change in one element, with the change direction spoken.
In the scrolling row VoiceOver moves card by card and scrolls the next one into view.
One column at accessibility text sizes, so values are never truncated.
edgeCases: An odd number of cards leaves the last grid row half filled; use an even number or the scrolling row.
Cards in one grid row take the height of the tallest; a long hint in one card makes its row taller.
Keep the figures to six or fewer; more belong in a report.

examples.title: Headline figures with changes
examples.setupTemplate:
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) private var dynamicTypeSize
examples.setup:
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) private var dynamicTypeSize
examples.code:
LazyVGrid(
    columns: Array(
        repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: theme.spacing.space3),
        count: dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 1 : 2
    ),
    spacing: theme.spacing.space3
) {
    MonarchStatCard(
        "Open tickets",
        value: 128,
        change: MonarchMetricChange(0.12, comparison: "vs previous 30 days", goodDirection: .down),
        format: .number
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        "Within target",
        value: 0.94,
        change: MonarchMetricChange(0.02),
        format: .percent
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        "First reply",
        value: 42,
        unit: "min",
        change: MonarchMetricChange(-0.08, goodDirection: .down)
    )
    MonarchStatCard("Satisfaction", value: nil, hint: "No survey answers yet")
}
.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
.accessibilityLabel("Last 30 days")
